title: When I kept silent (Psalm 32)
hookLine: holding a wrong in, my bones wasted away; confessing, I was forgiven

lines: A CHART OF A GUILTY CONSCIENCE.
cards: A sharp word to a friend, three weeks back. Credit taken for something that wasn't quite yours. A small lie, then another to cover it.
Nobody found out. And yet it sits there, at night, in the shoulders, in the stomach. Something that small, held in, can get heavy.
Long ago, someone wrote that weight down in a psalm that reads almost like a medical chart of a guilty conscience.

teach.b: Psalm thirty-two starts at the end of the story, with relief, in the King James Bible: "Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered." Then it goes back to tell how it got there.

"When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long. For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer." Bones aging. Groaning all day.
Dried out, like a field in August. The silence wasn't peaceful. It was exhausting.

teach.h: I SAID I WILL, AND THOU FORGAVEST.
teach.b: Then the turn, and it comes fast: "I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin."
I said I will confess, and you forgave. A weight carried for who knows how long lifts in a single breath.
Then God speaks: "I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye."

teach.h: NOT LIKE A HORSE OR A MULE.
teach.b: And a gentle warning: don't be like a horse or a mule that has to be steered with a bit and bridle. Paul quotes its opening in his letter to the Romans.
Western Christian tradition groups it with the penitential psalms, the psalms of turning back.

teach.h: WHEN I KEPT SILENCE, MY BONES WAXED OLD.
teach.b: Augustine's biographer says that as he was dying, Augustine had the penitential psalms copied and put on the wall where he could read them from his bed. Christians practice confession differently.
Catholics and Orthodox Christians confess to a priest in a sacrament.
Some Protestants confess directly to God, some in a prayer said together in church, and some to a trusted friend, as the letter of James puts it: confess your faults one to another.

how: Catholic and Orthodox Christians confess in the sacrament of reconciliation; some Protestants confess privately to God or in prayers of confession in worship. Psalm 32 is one of the penitential psalms, prayed in Lent in some churches.

o: psalms complaining about suffering that isn't fair
psalms written by prisoners serving a sentence
psalms of turning back to God after doing wrong

games.q: what's inside Psalm 32 — tap the pairs.

s: Psalm 32 says keeping quiet about a wrong brought peace
it brought exhaustion: bones aging, strength dried up like summer drought.
its opening, blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, appears in Romans 4.
all Christians confess sins the same way
Catholics and Orthodox confess to a priest; some Protestants confess directly to God, some to a friend.

games.q: you've been carrying a wrong in silence, and it's wearing you down. the psalmist was there too. what did he do?
o: kept quiet and waited for it to fade.
said, I will confess, and was forgiven.
made up for it with good deeds.
games.why: "I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin." one sentence, and the weight lifts.

practice: Let one small wrong you've been carrying in silence come to mind, not the biggest one, and notice where it sits in your body.
Then say it plainly: if you pray, to God, in your own words; if you don't, out loud to the empty room, or on a piece of paper. Then notice your shoulders.

wordCard.voice: Penitential psalms. The group of psalms, including this one, that the church prays when turning back to God after sin.

orig.note: Hebrew: I kept silent, from Psalm 32:3.

carryVoice: Your line: silence was heavy. One honest sentence, and it lifted. Day four hundred nineteen, done.
